transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-10-22
Start: 16:30 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Miguel Torres (Redwood SE), Sana Patel (Helix Head of ML), Evan Brooks (Platform Lead), Leila Gomez (Security Architect)

Summary: Short scoping to align on POC success criteria, workload sizing (chat vs embeddings), and decision criteria across Hosted, Dedicated, Private. Agreed to run a 2-week benchmark with Helix traces, pricing and security artifacts to be shared.

Topics Covered:
- Success criteria: latency, cost per 1M tokens, embedding throughput, quality/regression thresholds
- Workload sizing: expected QPS, typical prompt lengths, embedding volume
- Benchmarks: synthetic vs trace-driven, metrics, pass/fail thresholds
- Deployment decision drivers: data residency, SLA, predictable throughput, cost predictability, security controls
- Proposed pilot timeline and owners

---- Transcript ----
00:00 Alex (Redwood): okay everyone thanks for joining, um let's do a quick 1 minute intros and then jump into what you all want from this poc scoping session.
00:12 Sana (Helix): hi, Sana here, Head of ML at Helix Financial. We're trying to pick deployment for our customer support assistant and an embeddings-based search index for transaction data. Key constraints: low latency for the chat path, and strict data residency for EU customers.
00:26 Evan (Helix): Evan, platform, I'll be the infra contact. Main question for us is whether we go Hosted to move fast or insist on Dedicated/Private for predictability and compliance.
00:36 Alex (Redwood): great, thanks. Priya and Miguel from our side will cover benchmarks and runtime behavior. Quick agenda: load profile, success criteria, then map to Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs.
00:48 Priya (Redwood SE): mm-hmm. Sana, can you give ballpark numbers: qps for chat, token lengths, and embedding volume? even approximate helps.
00:58 Sana (Helix): sure. Chat: peak 80 qps, average 20 qps. Typical prompt+response ~300 tokens, tail p95 spikes to 1k tokens on long context. Embeddings: batch offline upsert ~50k vectors/day, real-time similarity calls ~50 qps at low latency.
01:20 Miguel (Redwood): ok that's helpful. For 80 qps and 300 tokens that's a mixed load — need to tune batching and cache. If you want p95 < 150-200 ms for short responses, we have to consider model size and routing.
01:33 Leila (Helix): security: all EU data must stay in EU region, we require KMS integration, audit logs, and SOC2 type 2 or ISO 27001 -- is that available for Hosted?
01:45 Alex (Redwood): yes our Hosted API has EU regions and SOC2, but for some customers we do Dedicated or Private to give stronger isolation and customer-managed KMS. We'll share the security pack after the call.
01:57 Sana (Helix): good. Also quality is critical — we will validate the assistant against a closed test set (10k prompts) and expect no regression vs baseline.
02:07 Priya (Redwood SE): makes sense. For the POC we'll propose metrics: latency (p50/p95/p99), throughput (tokens/sec and requests/sec), cost per 1M tokens, and a quality metric (top-1 similarity/accuracy on your eval set).
02:21 Evan (Helix): what's realistic for environment setup time? If we go Dedicated, how long to get capacity?
02:29 Miguel (Redwood): Dedicated provisioning usually 3-5 business days once contract signed if capacity available; Private (on-prem or VPC) has longer lead—can be 4-8 weeks depending on networking and KMS integrations. Hosted is immediate for development.
02:43 Sana (Helix): ok. For the benchmark, we want to measure cold start vs warm path, and kv-cache hit rate since we expect many repeated patterns.
02:52 Priya (Redwood SE): yes we'll include cold/warm runs and a KV cache hit simulation. We also recommend running quantized model variants to measure quality vs token-cost tradeoffs. Note: some higher quantization can affect instruction-following.
03:07 Leila (Helix): about encryption — Helix requires customer KMS for key separation. Hosted can you integrate our KMS or does that require Dedicated/Private?
03:16 Alex (Redwood): Hosted can support customer-managed keys via cloud KMS in some cases but Dedicated/Private offers more control (HSM/KMS at customer network boundary). We'll clarify exact limitations in the security pack.
03:27 Sana (Helix): can you explain routing/fallbacks? we want a plan if capacity is constrained.
03:33 Miguel (Redwood): routing policies: we can route by latency SLO, cost tier, or region. For example, primary to Dedicated pool and fallback to smaller Hosted model variant — with automatic graceful degradation. We'll include a proposed policy for Helix.
03:47 Evan (Helix): nice. On cost: we need predictable unit economics. Hosted may fluctuate; Dedicated gives committed cost but requires sizing accuracy. How do you recommend sizing for Dedicated?
03:59 Priya (Redwood SE): we'll run an initial sizing exercise in the benchmark phase: run your traces through a simulator to estimate GPU-hours, peak concurrency, and batching efficiency. We'll convert that into a recommended pool size and expected p95 latency.
04:12 Sana (Helix): what's a realistic POC length to get meaningful results?
04:16 Alex (Redwood): two options: a narrow Hosted-only 4-week POC to validate latency/quality quickly, or a 6-8 week POC if you want a Dedicated/Private full integration and security review. For contractual/enterprise customers we usually do 6 weeks for Dedicated.
04:32 Evan (Helix): we likely need the full Dedicated evaluation. Security signoff is a blocker for production.
04:36 Leila (Helix): yes. Also need proof of the audit log fidelity and retention guarantees.
04:42 Alex (Redwood): noted — we'll include sample audit log schema and retention options.

(roughly 20 minutes of technical discussion, timestamps sparse for brevity)

24:15 Priya (Redwood SE): going into benchmark details — propose we run two phases: Phase A (trace replay): run a representative 72-hour trace to get latency/throughput numbers; Phase B (stress tests): synthetic peak storm tests to validate tail latency and autoscale behavior.
24:32 Sana (Helix): phase A is critical — we'll send 72 hours of anonymized traces. How do you handle exfiltration / privacy for traces?
24:40 Alex (Redwood): we can do the benchmark in your VPC (Private) or in our Hosted EU region with contractual NDAs and data-delete guarantees. If traces contain sensitive fields we'll agree on scrub rules and can run hashed or tokenized versions.
24:55 Evan (Helix): preferred: run in our dev VPC or Redwood's Dedicated test pool. We'll confirm with infra.
25:01 Miguel (Redwood): for metrics: we'll capture p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, request/sec, batch sizes, KV cache hit %, and model quality metrics from your eval set. We'll also capture cost per estimated 1M tokens by variant and quantization level.
25:19 Sana (Helix): for quality threshold, we propose: no >5% drop in top-1 retrieval MRR on embeddings, and assistant must meet 0.85 similarity threshold on core intents.
25:31 Priya (Redwood SE): good, we'll attach metric collection code and example dashboards.
25:36 Leila (Helix): any red flags with PCI or transaction data in embeddings?
25:41 Alex (Redwood): sensitive fields should be tokenized or removed; for regulatory data we recommend Dedicated or Private so you control storage. We'll include recommended redaction patterns.
25:53 Sana (Helix): what about model variants — do you recommend auto-fallback to smaller models when under heavy load?
26:00 Miguel (Redwood): yes, we can configure model variants and automatic fallback policies that route to cheaper variants or cached responses under load to preserve availability. But note quality tradeoffs.
26:10 Evan (Helix): ok. Let's talk timelines and owners — if we aim for a 6-week Dedicated POC starting 2025-11-03, what are the milestones?
26:20 Alex (Redwood): proposed timeline: Week 0 (kickoff + procurement signatures), Week 1 (env setup, infra networking, KMS hookup), Week 2 (benchmarks phase A - trace replay), Week 3 (stress & tuning), Week 4 (quality eval & regressions), Week 5 (security review & audit artifacts), Week 6 (final review + decision). We'll be flexible.
26:44 Sana (Helix): procurement needs pricing and terms to start.
26:48 Alex (Redwood): we'll send a tailored quote for a 3-month Dedicated pilot and a Hosted fallback quote. That'll include model compute estimates from the sizing exercise.
26:58 Priya (Redwood SE): technical items I need from Helix: anonymized 72hr traces, small eval set (10k prompts) and embedding corpus sample (5k vectors) — ideally by 2025-10-23 so we can prepare.
27:16 Evan (Helix): we'll try to get that over by Friday.
27:20 Leila (Helix): security team will need the SOC2 packet and the detailed audit log schema.
27:27 Alex (Redwood): we'll share those by Monday 2025-10-27.

(Closing minutes)
49:10 Alex (Redwood): quick recap: action items and owners — Alex to send pricing and security docs; Priya to produce benchmark plan; Helix to send traces and evals. We'll target a kickoff the week of 2025-11-03 pending contract.
49:30 Sana (Helix): thanks team, this was helpful. We'll confirm internal stakeholders and timeline.
49:38 Evan (Helix): thanks.
49:40 Miguel (Redwood): thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invites for benchmark windows.

End of call.

Notes on transcription fidelity: occasional mis-heard phrases (e.g., "KV cache" transcribed as "K V cash"), some timestamps approximate.

POC success criteria (agreed):
- Latency: p95 for typical chat responses under standard load <= 200 ms (goal 150 ms)
- Throughput: sustain peak 80 qps with tail targets maintained
- Embeddings: real-time similarity calls <= 50 ms p95 for single-vector lookups; batch upsert throughput meeting 50k/day SLA
- Quality: <5% regression on embedding MRR, >=0.85 similarity on eval set
- Security: EU data residency, KMS integration for encryption-at-rest, audit log retention policy met

Benchmarks to run:
- Phase A: 72hr trace replay (capture p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, cache hit)
- Phase B: synthetic stress tests for autoscale and tail latency
- Variant matrix: baseline model, quantized variant, smaller cost-optimized model for fallback

Pilot timeline (proposed):
- Prep: by 2025-10-27 deliver security pack + quote
- Kickoff: target week of 2025-11-03
- 6-week Dedicated POC with milestones (setup, trace replay, stress, quality eval, security review, final decision)

References & artifacts to be shared:
- Redwood: SOC2 & ISO packet, audit log schema, proposed routing policy, benchmark plan and ingestion scripts
- Helix: anonymized traces, eval prompt set, embedding sample corpus

Action items (flat list):
- Alex Kim: pricing & security pack (due 2025-10-24)
- Priya Shah: benchmark plan + metric dashboard (due 2025-10-24)
- Evan Brooks: export anonymized traces & corpus (due 2025-10-23)
- Leila Gomez: confirm retention and KMS constraints (due 2025-10-27)

Questions left open:
- exact legal terms for Hosted KMS integration (Alex to confirm with legal)
- whether Helix infra team prefers Dedicated test pool or dev VPC for running the trace replay
